Exploitation without full relief is Zang et al.'s prestress, which switches stability while some transitions stay unachievable. In [TERM-060](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-060.md)'s sense only the first touches frustration; the others act on its load and its consequences. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CLAIM-600](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) v10 | Transient support can be withdrawn safely only if it started a process that keeps itself going on a flux that will stay available, was large enough to carry the supported party past any threshold that process has, outlasted the threat it stood in for, and left the work to the party throughout, in each subtask it must later do alone and not only in its role as a whole, at no more effort than it could bear, and, where the capacity is cumulative and its field moves fast, kept up after withdrawal; inputs the party cannot produce must stay supplied as a standing part of the arrangement; support that fails these leaves dependence or decay, but meeting them all is not enough, since support can carry a function nobody names before withdrawal; and persistence after withdrawal is needed to tell which, though slow reversion can mimic it | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to characterize "what differentiates transient support that induces dependency and is hazardous to remove from transient support that builds new capabilities and is safe to remove", with reintroduction and ecological recovery proposed as cases. It draws together the branch's three domains: DNA origami, aid and development, and ecology. Three conditions are needed for it. First, the support starts a self-sustaining process on an ambient flux instead of doing the upkeep. Planted tree islands, weeded for 2.5 years, kept their advantage to 16–18 years because established trees keep drawing seed dispersers (Holl et al.; Schubert et al.). Supplied repair, by contrast, never becomes optional ([CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md)). Second, the threat it stood in for is gone. Conservation-reliant species stay reliant while fire is suppressed or habitat threats persist (Mussmann et al.; Brown et al.). Third, the party did the work throughout. Support that does the work wears capacity down by disuse ([CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)), by slack effort (Ostrom et al.) or by selection for the supported conditions, which costs hatchery steelhead fitness in the wild within one generation (Christie et al.). Captive-bred translocated stock shows negative population growth (Morris et al.). Persistence must be shown after withdrawal: impact at exit and judged success both overstate it. Revised the same day after two counterpoints the owner asked for. Evidence against the lazy-poor stereotype finds no slack effort in poor households: cash transfers barely change work, and one-off graduation packages raise it. So that route is confined to help that is assured and permanent. A household asset threshold (Balboni et al.) adds a condition on size: support too small decays with no dependence at all. Urban development adds three cautions. Some public inputs are a standing part of a coproduced service (Evans; Watson). Forty years of persistence can be slow reversion (Kline and Moretti). And a place can last while the people it served are dispersed (Collins and Shester; LaVoice). The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. Moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme on 2026-11-07 ([ADR-077](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md)) and returned to CLAIM on 2026-11-08 (ADR-084), keeping the standing the status review of 2026-11-06 gave it under the rulings the owner delegated. | Active |
| [CLAIM-601](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-601.md) v4 | A savings buffer is a stock of time: where shocks must be absorbed or a household is ruined, an investment that pays only after a delay is worth taking only above a buffer that rises with the delay, so households with the same preferences decline profitable delayed investments below it, a choice that reads as impatience and is the right policy for survival by a deadline; covering needs through the delay buys the time | The assistant's, after the owner read Haushofer and Fehr's finding, that deprivation produces short-sighted choices, as decision-making under a resource constraint: "deprivation induces added time pressure to the decision making process." In [TERM-105](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-105.md)'s terms a savings buffer is a replenishable reserve, and its depth sets a deadline: how many bad seasons the household can absorb before ruin. A toy shows the consequence. Savings move +1 or −1 each period, and the household can pay 3 now for 6 later. Investing raises survival over 40 periods only above a buffer of 4 when the payoff comes after 1 period, rising to 5, 6, 9 and 14 at delays of 4, 9, 16 and 25. Below it, declining is right. Survival, the objective deprivation makes binding, needs a deeper buffer than expected wealth. At delay 16 and buffer 8, investing raises expected wealth from 8.15 to 10.30 and lowers survival from 0.846 to 0.835. Covering shocks through the delay lowers the threshold to the outlay alone, which is what graduation programmes' consumption support does. The time pressure here is the planning horizon. Deliberation time and attention are a second sense, left to the scarcity readings. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) v5 | Where an organization's capacity is learned by doing the work it serves, and decays with disuse, outside supply that does the work first lowers the capacity kept, and the longer it does all of it the longer recovery takes once it stops, while supply that covers only what the organization cannot yet do leaves its learning untouched, so what decides dependence is the order in which supply and capacity are used, not the amount of supply | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to look to aid and development for theory on how aid-dependent organizations become self-sufficient. [CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md) holds an outside supply that repairs the organization and leaves its own capacity alone. The readings say aid does not leave it alone: it does the work the capacity is learned from. Moss, Pettersson and van de Walle cite Kaldor, that a state leaves aid dependency as it "learns how to tax". Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's 1999 model already has taxing experience built by revenue collected and decaying with time, and capacity kept lower the more aid finances. Moore says raising revenue keeps a state's machinery alive at the grassroots. Ostrom et al. find recipients losing skill and rebuilding plants they did not maintain, and Andrews, Pritchett and Woolcock find capability stagnating under aid. In a model where capacity grows with the work done and decays with disuse ([CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)), aid that does a share A of the work first holds capacity at λ(1 − A)/(λ(1 − A) + μ): with λ = 1, μ = 0.3, 0.769 without aid, 0.625 at A = 0.5, 0.25 at 0.9 and none at full substitution. After full substitution for 10, 20 and 40 time units, meeting demand takes 3.8, 6.4 and 11.4 units once aid stops, because the work an organization can do is capped by its capacity, so it regrows from a seed. Aid used after capacity, covering only what it cannot yet do, keeps service whole and leaves capacity to grow as if there were no aid. The first point is Azam et al.'s; the second and third are not in their paper. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CLAIM-603](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) v8 | A capability lost because another reliably supplies it is the Black Queen's loss, favoured to the one who loses it, and whether it is dependency or division of labour is decided by the supply, not the loss: one-way supply set from outside, as aid is, leaves a dependence that nothing in the dependent's dynamics limits and that withdrawal punishes, while reciprocal loss, each partner supplying what the other gave up, leaves interdependence, so the aim framed as self-sufficiency is better framed as reciprocity | The assistant's, on the owner's remark of 2026-11-05 that "assured help makes recipients lose skill" sounds "closely related to niche differentiation and specialization phenomena". The record holds the biology. On the Black Queen Hypothesis ([THEORY-1048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md)) a cell that stops making a leaky public good saves its cost while others still supply it, so the loss is favoured to the individual and spreads. Buchnera ([THEORY-1103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1103.md)) has lost the genes its host covers and kept those its host lacks. The Samaritan's dilemma has the same logic (Ostrom et al.), and Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's recipient is better off in the high-aid state. The loss itself is not the pathology. What differs is the supply. A Black Queen loss stops by itself when helpers grow rare, because the helpers are the same population. Aid is set from outside and does not fall as dependence grows, so nothing stops the loss short of what aid covers, and withdrawal returns the cost ([CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md)). Buchnera's loss runs both ways, and the result is interdependence. A state that taxes its citizens (Moore) is in the same position: it lost nothing, it exchanges. After the owner linked the claim to the gift economy of Burning Man, readings of Mauss, of St John on Burning Man and of Heins, Unrau and Avram added two things. One-way supply costs the receiver standing as well as capacity: in Mauss the unreturned gift makes its receiver inferior. And the return need not go back to the giver: it can travel round a circuit, as Mauss's do, or out to a whole community, as Burning Man's is meant to, and both sit beside a demand for self-reliance. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-605](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md) v5 | Where capacity is learned by doing, decays with disuse and needs capacity already present to grow, support that does the work has a deadline after which withdrawal no longer restores capacity, and a slow taper of such support is worse than an abrupt cut because it holds practice down long enough to cross the threshold; support that covers only what the party cannot yet do needs no taper but cannot lift a party already below the threshold | The assistant's, filling gaps the supplied-maintenance filing left, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to "proceed systematically filling all of those identified gaps". [CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) modelled crowding out with no threshold, so capacity always regrew from a seed. Its own limits named the threshold case, Azam et al.'s trap. Here learning by doing needs capacity already present, dC/dt = λPC(1 − C) − μC. With λ = 1, μ = 0.3 and τ = 1.5, a party alone keeps C = 0.7, and C below 0.276 decays to nothing. The model gives three results. Support that does all the work has a deadline: after ln(0.7/0.276)/0.3 = 3.10 time units capacity has crossed the threshold, and withdrawal no longer restores it. Tapering such support is worse the slower it is: from C = 0.45 under support doing 95 % of the work, an abrupt cut recovers, a taper over 5 periods recovers, and any taper longer than 9.13 periods traps the party. Capacity-first support needs no taper, since it withdraws itself, but it cannot lift a party already below the threshold. That reconciles Azam et al.'s optimal up-front cut, made for substitutive aid, with the Kenya exit study's success with gradual exits in which participants already did the work. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |

| [CLAIM-669](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-669.md) v7 | An arrangement can exploit through the access it grants: a needed good offered on terms that leave the recipient with a lasting encumbrance, a reliance on the provider or an obligation hard to escape, that narrows later exit or renegotiation, so that exploitation can arise through inclusion that succeeds, not only through inclusion that fails, and widening access need not reduce it | A's, from A9 §2 of the exchange "About Plantation Paradise" (2026-11-12), narrowed to its version 2 after Seamster and Charron-Chénier's "predatory inclusion" was read ([NOTE-1902](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1902.md); [ARG-100](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-100.md)). | [CLAIM-671](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-671.md) v8 | Where an organizational transformation increases a constituent's vulnerability to the discretionary choices of a responsible agent, and that vulnerability grounds special obligations under an independently justified principle, the transformation can strengthen that agent's responsibilities toward the constituent | The proposition stated in the owner's review of [#488](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/488) on 2026-11-13, replacing A's (A12 §1 and §10 of the exchange "About Plantation Paradise", 2026-11-12: "The whole's responsibilities could therefore grow as its integration deepens"). | [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md) v6 | Two forms of support that give a party the same capabilities now can leave it different capabilities later: where capacity is learned by doing and decays with disuse, support that does the work shrinks what the party can reach unaided while support that covers only its shortfall does not, so support, or a technology, cannot be ranked by present capability sets and has to be assessed by the capability trajectory it produces | A's, from the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13): A17 §V ("A technology can increase what someone accomplishes today while reducing what they will be capable of accomplishing tomorrow"; "We should investigate how particular forms of assistance change the person's future capability trajectory") and A23 §6 ("We therefore need to evaluate capability trajectories, not merely present capability sets"), joining [CLAIM-605](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md)'s capability trap to Sen's capability approach as [CLAIM-352](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-352.md) reads it. | [CLAIM-678](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-678.md) v5 | Power over a technological arrangement has at least three dimensions that can be held and distributed separately: operational power, over how it works; economic power, over who owns it and takes its benefits; and epistemic power, over the knowledge needed to understand, evaluate and challenge it; so widening one, by public ownership, consumer choice or technical literacy, does not of itself widen the others | A's, from A11 §5 of the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13), drawing on Mumford, Feenberg and Zuboff: "we should examine technological power in three dimensions", operational ("Who determines how the system works?"), economic ("Who owns the assets and captures the benefits?") and epistemic ("Who possesses the knowledge needed to understand, evaluate, and challenge it?"). | [CLAIM-686](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-686.md) v5 | Where a dependent party's claims on an arrangement's controllers fail of legibility, volitional efficacy or correctability in the controlling organization, the dependent lacks effective means of influence and challenge, and where they fail so at every party able to constrain the controllers it lacks effective protection; justified withdrawal lies outside those three achievements, so the domination threshold's third condition is met by failures of normative efficacy only together with a failure of exit, and is not those failures restated | The assistant's, from the step-12 ideas of the filing of the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13), offered as "the threshold in the record's own terms" and accepted by the owner on 2026-11-13 ("file the still unfiled stuff").
